{{Infobox football league season | competition= [[Elite One]] | season= 2019–20 | image= | dates= 18 October 2019 – 16 March 2020 | winners= [[PWD Bamenda]] (first [[Elite One]] title) | relegated= [[Dragon Club (Yaoundé)|Dragon Club de Yaoundé]] | continentalcup1= [[2020–21 CAF Champions League|Champions League]] | continentalcup1 qualifiers= [[PWD Bamenda]] | continentalcup2= [[2020–21 CAF Confederation Cup|Confederation Cup]] | continentalcup2 qualifiers= [[Coton Sport FC de Garoua|Coton Sport]] | matches= 306 | total goals= 522 | biggest home win= [[Coton Sport FC de Garoua|Coton Sport]] 6–1 [[Yong Sports Academy]] (24 October 2019) [[Coton Sport FC de Garoua|Coton Sport]] 5–0 [[PWD Bamenda]] (11 November 2019) | biggest away win= [[Eding Sport FC|Eding Sport]] 1–5 [[:es:Feutcheu FC|Feutcheu FC]] (5 February 2020) [[Dragon Club (Yaoundé)|Dragon Club]] 0–4 [[AS Fortuna]] (12 March 2020) | highest scoring= [[:es:Colombe Sportive|Colombe Sportive]] 2–5 [[Bamboutos FC|Bamboutos]] (18 October 2019) [[Coton Sport FC de Garoua|Coton Sport]] 6–1 [[Yong Sports Academy]] (24 October 2019) | longest wins=[[:es:Colombe Sportive|Colombe Sportive]] (5 matches) | longest unbeaten= [[Bamboutos FC|Bamboutos]] & [[Tonnerre Yaoundé]] (11 matches) | longest winless= [[AS Fortuna Mfou]] (12 matches) | longest losses= [[Tonnerre Yaoundé]] (6 matches) | prevseason= [[2019 Elite One|2019]] | nextseason= [[2020–21 Elite One|2020–21]] | updated= 16 March 2020 }} The '''2019–20 Elite One''' was the 60th season of the [[Elite One]], the top-tier [[association football|football]] league in [[Cameroon]]. This was the first season in the [[Elite One]] to use an October–May schedule since the 2011–12 season, it was changed so as to conform with the new [[Confederation of African Football|CAF]] calendar.{{cite news |title=Local clubs to be affected by CAF calendar changes |url=https://www.soccer24.co.zw/2018/07/24/local-clubs-affected-caf-calendar-changes/ |work=Soccer24 |access-date=29 June 2020}} The season started on 18 October 2019 and was scheduled to end on 26 April 2020, but due to the effects of the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Cameroon|COVID-19 pandemic]], the season was cancelled on 12 May 2020 by [[Cameroonian Football Federation|FECAFOOT]].{{cite news | title= PWD Bamenda crowned champions as FECAFOOT cancels season |url=https://www.goal.com/en-ug/news/coronavirus-pwd-bamenda-crowned-cameroonian-champions-after/1uz329qmqptax11xzokvuf20wg |work= Goal.com |access-date= 18 June 2020}} [[PWD Bamenda]] won their first [[Elite One]] silverware as they were crowned champions, alongside [[Coton Sport FC de Garoua|Coton Sport]], they will represent [[Cameroonian Football Federation|Cameroon]] at the 2020–21 [[2020–21 CAF Champions League|CAF Champions League]] and [[2020–21 CAF Confederation Cup|CAF Confederation Cup]] respectively as the [[Cameroonian Cup]] won't hold this year. Only [[Dragon Club (Yaoundé)|Dragon Club]] were relegated to the [[Elite Two]] as the teams would be increased to twenty teams during the next season. There were no Championship and Relegation group this season. ==Teams== Eighteen teams competed in the league, the top 15 teams from the [[2019 Elite One|previous season]] and the three promoted teams from the [[Elite Two]] ([[Bamboutos FC]], [[Canon Yaoundé|Canon Sportif]] and [[Panthère du Ndé]]) while ([[PWD Bamenda]], [[New Star de Douala]] and [[Unisport FC de Bafang]]) relegated from the previous season after finishing last at the playoffs.{{cite news |title=What future relegated for New Stars of Douala, PWD Bamenda and Unisport of Bafang |url=https://www.kick442.com/what-future-relegated-for-new-stars-of-douala-pwd-of-bamenda-and-unisport-of-bafang/ |work=[[Kick442.com]] |access-date=18 June 2019 }}{{Dead link|date=September 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }} [[PWD Bamenda]] later replaced [[Les Astres FC]].
